title: Rydberg-mediated microwave-to-optical transduction with tunable bandwidth
authors: Iason Tsiamis, David Petrosyan, Anders S. Sørensen
abstract: Coherent microwave-to-optical transduction is essential for hybrid quantum networks. Typical transducers, however, have bandwidths set by fixed device parameters and face efficiency-bandwidth tradeoffs. We propose a cavity-based microwave-to-optical transducer mediated by a collective Rydberg excitation, where external driving fields tune the conversion bandwidth in situ from narrowband, spectrally selective operation to broadband operation without modifying cavity parameters. Under impedance-matching conditions, the system operates as a continuous-wave phase-preserving linear transducer, maintaining both near-unit efficiency and quantum-limited added noise throughout the tunable bandwidth range.
summary: This paper presents a theoretical model for a microwave-to-optical transducer using Rydberg atoms, addressing the limitation of fixed bandwidths in current devices. By tuning external driving fields, the system's conversion bandwidth can be continuously controlled from narrow to broadband while maintaining near-unit efficiency. This offers a powerful tool for building versatile quantum network components.
main_problem: Coherent microwave-to-optical transduction is crucial for quantum networks, but existing transducers suffer from fixed bandwidths and efficiency-bandwidth tradeoffs.
main_result: The authors propose a Rydberg-mediated transducer whose conversion bandwidth can be continuously tuned in situ from narrowband to broadband without altering the physical cavity parameters.
method: The analysis uses the Heisenberg-Langevin equations and input-output relations to derive the conversion amplitude and efficiency, modeling the system dynamics in an effective three-mode Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system involves an ensemble of Rydberg atoms coupled to microwave and optical cavities. The dynamics are modeled by adiabatically eliminating intermediate states to derive an effective Hamiltonian describing coupling between a collective spin-wave mode and the two cavity modes.
key_observables: Conversion efficiency $\eta(\omega)$, conversion bandwidth ($\Delta\omega$), and the spectral response $S_{o\mu}(\omega)$.
important_parameters: Impedance-matching condition ($\Gamma_\mu = \Gamma_o$), driving field ratios ($\Omega_1/\Delta$, $\Omega_2/\delta_s$), and the ratio of cavity linewidths ($r = \kappa_\mu / \kappa_o$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on operating in the far-off-resonant regime and assuming weak excitation to allow for adiabatic elimination of certain atomic states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral response changing from a narrow resonance to a broadened, flat response as coupling parameters increase, and show efficiency/bandwidth dependence on linewidth ratios and coupling strengths.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the necessity of tunable transduction, develops the effective Hamiltonian via state elimination, derives the spectral response, and then analyzes the tunability and robustness of the high-efficiency, broadband regime.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for engineering quantum interfaces, demonstrating how external driving fields can dynamically control the spectral properties of quantum transducers, which is highly relevant for quantum network architectures.
